title: Privacy-preserving audit hash protocol proposal
body:
Context:
We need a way to provide customers and auditors tamper-evident proof that a tenant's requests and data were served from a pinned region (or not moved across borders) without exposing PII or full request payloads to auditors or storing raw payload copies in the control plane. Existing evidence specs (routing traces, SLA bundles) are useful but often reveal too much or are operationally heavy to produce on-demand for audits.

Goal (high level):
- Produce compact, verifiable artifacts that demonstrate region residency for a time window, with cryptographic integrity and minimal data exposure.
- Support both automated customer requests and third-party audits.
- Be feasible to generate in Dedicated and Private deployments where customers care about data locality and minimal shared-surface.

Core idea summary:
- For each served request (or batch window), compute a short, salted hash commitment instead of storing payloads.
- Build periodic Merkle trees over commitments per-tenant-per-region, sign the Merkle root with a region-local key (KMS/HSM).
- Publish signed roots and an append-only index (time-ordered) that auditors can verify; on-demand provide inclusion proofs for specific commitment hashes.
- Commitments are deterministic over redacted representation to balance privacy and verifiability (see "representation" below).

Representation used for commitment (draft):
- canonicalize(request_meta) + canonicalize(region_assertion) + tenant_id + minimal fingerprint(payload)
- Where minimal fingerprint(payload) = H(salt || redaction(payload))
- redaction(payload) strategy is configurable: e.g., remove tokens > 8 chars, strip free text, keep headers and routing fields. Purpose: preserve ability to prove request existed without revealing content.
- salt per-tenant stored in HSM/KMS; per-period rotation possible.

Merkle / signing cadence options (tradeoffs):
- Per-minute roots (fine-grained, larger index, faster inclusion proofs) — higher CPU/storage for proofs
- Per-hour roots (coarser, smaller index) — less operational cost but slower proofs and larger batch sizes
- Default: hourly roots with option for customers to opt into per-minute if they need high-res audit.

Key management & trust model:
- Region-local signing key stored in a KMS-backed HSM that never leaves the region (for Private/VPC deployments use customer-managed KMS where available).
- Signatures include: region-id, tenant-id, time-window, root-hash, key-id, key-version.
- Verify flow: auditor/checker verifies signature (KMS-public-key), checks Merkle inclusion proof, then optionally requests commitment reveal (salted fingerprint) for a small set of IDs.

Proof reveal modes (privacy controls):
- Blind audit: only signed Merkle roots + inclusion proofs; no commitment reveals.
- Redacted reveal: operator provides redacted payload fingerprints and associated canonicalized metadata (no PII), sufficient to correlate with customer-provided request identifiers.
- Full reveal (rare, by legal/subpoena): provide raw request payload under strict controls (needs legal workstream).

Implementation sketch (operator steps):
1) At serve-time: generate request canonicalization and compute commitment = HMAC(salt, canonicalized-representation).
2) Append commitment to tenant-region append-only queue (local to region) with timestamp and minimal meta (route, model-id).
3) Periodically run Merkle-tree builder per-tenant-region window -> compute root, sign with region-local KMS.
4) Persist signed-root and inclusion index in immutable storage (WORM-compatible if possible). Create low-cost index for search by time-window + tenant.
5) Provide API endpoints: GET /audit/roots?tenant=...&from=...&to=..., GET /audit/proof?commitment=..., GET /audit/verify-root?root_id=...

Operational considerations / failure modes:
- Clock skew: signers must use monotonic time source; include server-provided epoch and allow small leeway when verifying.
- Queue loss: use durable local append-only stores with replication; if region-local builder can't complete (node failure), retain raw commitments for retry period before tombstone.
- Salt compromise: if tenant salt leaks, previously published commitments could be re-derived; mitigate via salt rotation and retention-limited proofs, and mark affected epochs in index.
- Legal subpoenas: process documented in legal runbook; this protocol reduces exposure by default but does not eliminate lawful data disclosure.

Acceptance criteria (for initial pilot):
- P0: signed roots generated hourly for pilot tenants in two regions; inclusion proofs verifiable by a small audit script.
- P1: API endpoints supporting root listing and proof retrieval; logs and telemetry for builder success rates, latencies.
- P2: salt rotation and KMS integration tested; key-rotation workflow documented.

Telemetry & metrics to track:
- roots_generated_per_window (success/fail)
- average_time_to_root (how long from first request to root signed)
- proof_generation_latency
- commitments_queue_size_per_tenant_region
- salt_rotation_events
- auditor_api_calls (rate-limited)

Rollout plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (lab): prototype builder in staging, use synthetic requests, verify end-to-end verify script.
- Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 2-3 pilot tenants in Dedicated (non-customer-managed KMS) and 1 Private deployment with CMK, collect feedback.
- Phase 2 (gradual opt-in): provide self-serve toggle in Console / API; document limitations and TTL for proofs.
- Phase 3 (GA): default enable for enterprise customers with compliance needs; add per-minute option and compliance SLAs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- canonicalization rules: need a concrete spec + tests. How to handle attachments/binary blobs? (proposal: hash blob separately and include size/type only)
- retention windows: legal teams want 7 years for some audits — storing proofs that long has cost implications.
- inclusion transparency: should roots be published to a public transparency log (like CT) for extra tamper-evidence? Some customers may object.
- customer-supplied salts: for Private deployments, should we require customer-managed salts (CMK) or allow Redwood-managed with attestation?
- UX: what identifiers will customers provide to match their internal logs? Need mapping doc + sync plan.

Quick implementation checklist (dev tasks):
- [ ] define canonicalization spec and test vectors
- [ ] implement commitment generator library (Rust/Go/Py)
- [ ] implement region-local append-only queue (durable, small footprint)
- [ ] implement Merkle builder and signer integration with KMS
- [ ] implement audit API endpoints and minimal verifier CLI
- [ ] write operator runbook for salt rotation and incident handling

Notes-to-self / brainstorming snippets:
- Could use small BLS aggregated signatures if we want single-signed root across multiple region nodes, but KMS support is trickier.
- Consider storing only signed roots in global control plane and keep inclusion indices region-local to avoid cross-border movement of proof index data.
- For customer visibility: show a compact "residency ledger" in Console with per-day counts + root fingerprints to reduce audit back-and-forth.

References / related docs:
- CONF-priv-audit-2025-1 (design brief)
- JIRA-RES-4123 (task: implement merkle builder)
- existing evidence spec: auditable-routing-evidence-spec-for-region-pins (see gaps re: privacy)

Next meeting agenda (sync):
- Review canonicalization proposal (Nora)
- KMS/HSM options & constraints for Private (Diego)
- Pilot tenant candidates and legal constraints (Liam + legal)
